story_type: tsunami ghost ship sunk by Coast Guard cutter gunfire
hook: A ghost ship drifted from Japan to Alaska. Then the guns opened up.
narration: This ghost ship drifted from Japan to Alaska with nobody aboard. Then a Coast Guard cutter opened fire.
The fishing vessel Ryou-Un Maru was set adrift by the earthquake and tsunami that struck Japan in 2011.
A year later, a Coast Guard plane found it unmanned and unlit, a hundred and seventy miles from Sitka.
A rusting hull with no lights and no crew is a collision waiting to happen for any ship that meets it at night.
On April fifth, 2012, the cutter Anacapa fired explosive rounds into the hull.
Black smoke poured out, and the crew kept firing to fill it with water.
[short pause] Then the stern rolled and started to go under.
outcome: The Ryou-Un Maru sank in six thousand feet of water, a hundred and eighty miles off Southeast Alaska.
title: Tsunami ghost ship sunk by gunfire
description:
The Coast Guard Cutter Anacapa sinks the Japanese fishing vessel Ryou-Un Maru, set adrift by the 2011 tsunami, in the Gulf of Alaska on April 5, 2012.

Footage: U.S. Coast Guard video by Petty Officer 2nd Class Brandon Thomas, via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/317555
